member: Dalia - Cooperative Use and Produce Preservation Specialist
message:
Amara, Baraka and Chidi, the tonne fits as fifty hand lifts moved in dated order.

Plainly two side racks with a middle walkway hold fifty vented crates stacked five high with air gaps, so one person carries one crate at a time and oldest leaves first. The count is 50 crates times 20 kg equals 1000 kg, with 600 by 400 mm footprints in the stacking crate source (E36) and 27.1 percent fill in the chamber simulation (E44), bedroom scale so air still moves.

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, spoilage stays low by sorting outside and checking daily.

Plainly damaged stock never enters, crates stay vented with gaps, and daily removal stops spread while holding chill moist air. The practice is remove defects and sell oldest first, First-In First-Out where First-In First-Out (FIFO) means oldest sold first, in the postharvest practices (E46), with brief openings of the 800 mm door in the seal detail sketch (E59), house-door scale so leakage stays small.

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, cleaning and lifting stay safe for cooperative hands.

Plainly smooth washable walls and floor drain let wash water leave without standing pools, and the single-crate limit keeps lifts safe. The lift is 20 kg in the floor pressure calculation (E43), luggage scale, spread to 2.04 kPa about one tenth of standing so ordinary. I am not ready, because the blocking energy mismatch objection (O1) on cooling and power is outside my ownership and must be cleared by Amara, Baraka and Chidi before a vote.
